messages:
devon: Quick q — trying to wire IRSA sa -> IAM role -> KMS grants for the secrets-agent. terraform apply sometimes creates the kms_grant before the role is usable and we see pods failing to decrypt. Anyone seen ordering weirdness or a better pattern?

marta: hmm, have you confirmed the pods are actually using the new serviceaccount annotation after deploy? IRSA needs the SA annotated and pods restarted. :thinking:

devon: yep — SA has `eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn` and I redeployed, but still intermittent decrypt failures. The terraform plan shows grant referencing the role ARN directly.

shreya: can you paste the relevant tf? small snippet is fine.

devon: sure:
```hcl
resource "aws_iam_role" "secrets_agent" {
  name = "secrets-agent-${var.env}"
  assume_role_policy = data.aws_iam_policy_document.irsa_sa.json
}

resource "aws_kms_key" "secrets" {
  description = "secrets key"
}

resource "aws_kms_grant" "sa_decrypt" {
  key_id = aws_kms_key.secrets.key_id
  grantee_principal = aws_iam_role.secrets_agent.arn
  operations = ["Decrypt"]
}
```

marta: TF will generate implicit dependencies when you reference attributes, but KMS grants can be funky if the IAM principal doesn't fully exist/propagate at the time AWS validates. Two common fixes: add an explicit depends_on on the grant pointing to the role, or modify the key policy to include the role ARN principal instead of relying only on grant.

alex: also check if this is cross-account. If the role is in a different account than the key, grants behave differently and key policy must allow the role principal. If same account, grants usually work but there can be eventual consistency delays.

shreya: I recently hit this — I added `depends_on = [aws_iam_role.secrets_agent]` on the `aws_kms_grant` and also a tiny `null_resource.wait_for_iam` with local-exec sleep(10) after role creation. Ugly but stabilized things. Better long-term: add the role ARN to the KMS key policy (explicit Principal statement) so the grant becomes just a convenience.

devon: good notes. Any preferred key policy pattern? I don't want to open it too wide.

marta: something like:
```json
{
  "Sid": "AllowSecretsAgentUse",
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::${data.aws_caller_identity.current.account_id}:role/secrets-agent-${var.env}"},
  "Action": ["kms:Decrypt", "kms:DescribeKey"],
  "Resource": "*"
}
```
That keeps it scoped to the role ARN. You can generate the exact ARN with `aws_iam_role.secrets_agent.arn`.

alex: if you create key policy with the role ARN, terraform needs to know the role ARN at plan time — using interpolation from the role resource works but be aware of the cycle if you also try to reference the key inside the role (we don't).

devon: thanks. One more wrinkle: we create one service account per namespace and a single key shared across namespaces. Is there any gotcha with using the same key + grants for multiple roles/serviceaccounts?

shreya: it's fine. You can attach multiple grants or add multiple principals to the key policy. Grants are ephemeral and have a creation time, but multiple grants -> multiple grantee_principal entries are normal. Key policy with multiple principal ARNs is easiest for long-term.

marta: FYI if you do grants for many roles, you may hit grant limits (not very common), so key policy is more scalable.

devon: ok actionable list: 1) try explicit depends_on on grant, 2) add conservative key policy principal for role ARN, 3) ensure pod rollout after SA annotation. I'll try in a sandbox.

alex: ping me if you want a quick review. also watch CloudTrail KMS events — failure reasons are usually descriptive (AccessDenied vs NotAuthorized).

k8s-deploy-bot: Deployment secrets-agent/1.3.7 started rolling on cluster prod-eu (triggered by devon)

devon: thanks all — i'll report back results here. :+1:
